subject: Generate null model for model fit comparison with bandit2arm_delta()

messages.author: 6403ad2aa9ae6d03
messages.subject: Generate null model for model fit comparison with bandit2arm_delta()
parts:
Hi all,

I'm an hBayesDM newbie, and I'm interested in comparing the model fit for a model produced by the bandit2arm_delta() function against a model in which subjects decide between the two choices at random (i.e., a null model in which there is no learning involved). My goal here is to compare these two models and foreclose on the hypothesis that subjects are simply making their choices randomly. My intuition is that the code for bandit2arm_delta() can be augmented to accomplish this, but I'm not exactly sure how. 

Does anyone have any idea how I might go about doing this, or otherwise have any suggestions? Thank you!

Best,

Thomas McCauley
Ph.D. student
Department of Psychology
University of California, San Diego

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Generate null model for model fit comparison with bandit2arm_delta()
parts:
Hi Thomas, 

Many apologies for the long delay!

Yes, you can make a model that assumes that participants make random choices

Here in line 52 (https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/534907d9cbe7101b3109feeec808cdbd380a93f2/commons/stan_files/bandit2arm_delta.stan#L52), 

you can find how a choice made. You can replace that line with a random sampling model based on Stan reference manual. 

You can replace 

choice[i, t] ~ categorical_logit(tau[i] * ev);

with 

random_ev = [1 1];   # same expected value for two options. This is just an example. There's other different ways to do this. 
choice[i, t] ~ categorical_logit(random_ev);


Let me know if this helps!

Best,
Young
